meta.projects.title: Custom Projects | Aaron Angel Netto
projects.title: Things I designed and built from zero
projects.lead: Every project here started as a problem with no off-the-shelf answer. Open a panel for the full story.
projects.cement.title: Custom Cement 3D Printer
projects.cement.summary: My major college engineering project: a cement-based 3D printer designed and built from scratch, covering the mechanical structure, motion, electronics and extrusion.
projects.cement.problem: Cement behaves nothing like thermoplastic. Material consistency, flow rate, extrusion pressure, nozzle geometry and layer deposition all had to be solved, and motion and material flow had to work as one system.
projects.cement.process: A BigTreeTech controller with stepper motors and drivers, a custom auger-based extruder and a peristaltic pump for material delivery, running Marlin firmware. Designed in FreeCAD and refined through repeated build, test and fix cycles.
projects.cement.result: A complete printer, built by hand, where the motion system and the cement flow work together to lay down layers.
projects.cement.quote: "I didn't just use a 3D printer. I built one for a material it was never designed to print."
projects.splint.title: Universal Mouldable Splint
projects.splint.summary: A splint printed flat on a standard printer, then heat-formed with hot water to fit the patient's limb.
projects.splint.problem: The idea came from a hospital visit. Casts are heavy and bulky, and one-size-fits-all splints rarely fit well.
projects.splint.process: A flat-bed-printable design that softens in hot water and is shaped directly on the limb. Explored in collaboration with Athira Hospital, Chavara, Kollam.
projects.splint.result: A splint that is lighter and less bulky than a cast, with adaptable geometry, designed for low-cost local fabrication.
projects.splint.note: A product-development concept, not a clinically validated medical device.
projects.guitar.title: 3D-Printed Electric Guitar
projects.guitar.summary: An original sci-fi, asymmetric, angular electric guitar designed in Autodesk Fusion.
projects.guitar.problem: A full guitar body is far bigger than a hobby print bed, and it has to survive string tension.
projects.guitar.process: A 20 × 40 mm aluminium T-slot extrusion runs from the body into the neck as the backbone. The body has hexagonal through-holes and is split into bolt-together modules that fit a 220 × 220 × 250 mm bed.
projects.guitar.result: The body is modelled. Spin it below. Next: printing and assembly.
common.viewerHint: Drag to rotate · scroll or pinch to zoom · double-click to reset
projects.arm.title: Gesture-Controlled Robotic Arm
projects.arm.summary: Built single-handedly: a robotic arm that follows hand gestures through computer vision.
projects.arm.problem: Control a robotic arm naturally, with your hand, without joysticks or a remote.
projects.arm.process: MediaPipe tracks 21 points on the hand, YOLOv8 handles detection, and an Arduino drives the motors.
projects.arm.result: An arm that responds to hand movements in real time.
meta.projects.desc: A cement 3D printer built from scratch, a mouldable splint, a 3D-printed electric guitar and a gesture-controlled robotic arm.

meta.about.title: About & Contact | Aaron Angel Netto
about.title: An engineer who learns by building
about.p1: I'm Aaron, an electronics & communication engineer from the College of Engineering Perumon in Kerala, living in Kuwait. I learn by building: when something doesn't exist, I design it; when something breaks, I take it apart until I understand it.
about.p2: My approach is always the same: identify a problem, learn what's needed, design, build, test and improve. That loop took me from a cement 3D printer to a print business that brought discontinued parts back, and through engines, lathes and circuit boards along the way.
about.p3: Outside the workshop there are the bikes, Ava and Toraa, and the guitar, where my first song is on its way. The chaos is what drives all of it.
